stats.title: 7 Behaviors That Quietly Signal You Have Class

structure.what_is_said: 'Have you ever met someone who didn't try to stand out... and yet everyone treated them with quiet respect? ... It's not what they're wearing, not what they're saying. It's how they move, how they respond, and what they choose not to do. Most of these behaviors are subtle, but once you notice them, you start seeing them everywhere.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: All FULL: royal at Wimbledon 0:00-0:03 -> YouTuber in fedora 0:03-0:09 (4 dissolves) -> classic film 0:10-0:15 -> celebrity interview 0:15-0:18 -> creator in a market 0:18-0:23 -> creator in white hat 0:23-0:28. No text, no captions.

structure.what_is_said: 'In today's video, we're uncovering seven behaviors that quietly signal high class. And while they may seem small, they quietly change how people see you and how they treat you. Let's begin.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: WHITE card 'In today's episode...' 0:28.5-0:32 -> FULL entrance clip with 'Episode 21' / '7 Signs You're High Class' 0:32-0:40 -> fade to white.

structure.what_is_said: 'You can tell a lot about someone in moments...'
structure.how_it_is_shown: '1. In Small Moments' on caramel that brightens to white.

structure.what_is_said: How you treat the person serving coffee, holding the door, a stranger; most people rush a thank-you; elegant people slow down, make eye contact, stay the same with everyone; people respect, trust and remember them.
structure.how_it_is_shown: WHITE+vertical -> ROW 3 built on 'coffee / door / stranger' -> FULL (water poured) -> FULL (sommelier) -> WHITE+photo -> ROW 2 -> CARAMEL split with quote text -> CARAMEL+vertical royal -> FULL friends -> FULL Capri.

structure.what_is_said: 'You've probably caught yourself doing this before.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: WHITE card '2. It's Not About Them'.

structure.what_is_said: Relating someone's story back to yourself shifts the focus; elegant people stay with the other person, listen longer, ask one more question; people want to feel heard; 'That's class.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: FULL dinner -> caramel -> FULL café -> FULL film (Mr. & Mrs. Smith-like, 2 shots) -> WHITE+vertical photos (2) -> FULL Alfredo restaurant -> FULL older friends -> FULL living-room talk.

structure.what_is_said: 'This one sounds simple, but it stands out more than you think. You say you'll send something. You say you'll'
structure.how_it_is_shown: WHITE card '3. They Do What They Say', ~7 s, text erases right to left.

structure.what_is_said: Life happens and we forget; someone who consistently follows through gets noticed; if they say it they do it, if something changes they let you know; that creates trust and ease.
structure.how_it_is_shown: FULL car x2 -> caramel -> ROW 3 (built from the middle) -> WHITE+vertical reels x2 -> CARAMEL split -> ROW 2.

structure.what_is_said: 'And if you'd like to discover what truly suits you and feel more effortlessly put together, the personal stylist guide is linked below. Sent instantly to your email after access.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: FULL chic outfit -> WHITE+vertical before/after reel ('Summer clothes don't look good on me...' / 'Not true.') -> FULL arcade clip with the 'Check the description for / Personal Stylist Guide / www.classyladyacademy.com' overlay.

structure.what_is_said: 'You've definitely seen this happen. Someone's telling a story, maybe a couple, maybe friends, and it's going well until there's that'
structure.how_it_is_shown: WHITE card '4. They Let It Slide', ~7 s.

structure.what_is_said: Narrator acts out corrections ('No, that's not how it happened...'); the story becomes a correction; elegant people notice and choose not to step in; not every detail needs correcting; keeping the moment smooth matters more than being right.
structure.how_it_is_shown: FULL older couple ~11 s -> WHITE -> FULL film argument (The Break-Up-like) -> FULL wine drinker -> ROW 3 built one by one -> FULL older women -> FULL couple -> CARAMEL+clip x2.

structure.what_is_said: 'Pay attention to this. How people talk about others when they're not around.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: WHITE card '5. They Speak Well of Others'.

structure.what_is_said: Gossip feels harmless but adds up; elegant people don't put others down or rely on negativity; they keep their tone respectful; people trust them more.
structure.how_it_is_shown: FULL royal -> WHITE + rounded frames (B&W gossip photo, Devil Wears Prada-like x2) -> FULL garden party -> ROW 3 -> ROW 2 -> CARAMEL + royal clip.

structure.what_is_said: 'They don't highlight small mistakes.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: WHITE card '6. They Overlook Small Things'.

structure.what_is_said: Someone says the wrong thing or spills something; the urge is to point it out; elegant people smooth it over, keep the conversation moving, make it easier for the other person; people feel comfortable.
structure.how_it_is_shown: FULL boat -> ROW 2 of stock reaction photos on white -> WHITE -> CARAMEL+clip (mother and son) -> FULL bedroom (2 shots) -> FULL terrace breakfast.

structure.what_is_said: 'Most of us say thank you quickly, automatically, and then we move on. But when someone slows that moment'
structure.how_it_is_shown: WHITE card '7. They Express Gratitude', ~7 s.

structure.what_is_said: Instead of a plain thank you: 'I really appreciated that. You didn't have to do that.' / 'That actually helped more than you think.' Elegant people make appreciation specific; it stays with people.
structure.how_it_is_shown: ROW 2 built -> CARAMEL split with the example sentences as quote text -> ROW 3 built.

structure.what_is_said: None of these are big changes; you don't have to get them all right; even one or two change how people experience you; real class isn't about being perfect, it's about intention and how you make people feel.
structure.how_it_is_shown: FULL creator -> FULL celebrity interview -> FULL creator by the sea -> CARAMEL split with 'Real class isn't about being perfect.' + 'It's about intention.' (script).

structure.what_is_said: 'I'm curious. Which of these felt the most natural to you? And which one made you pause for a second? Because sometimes it's not about becoming someone new. It's about noticing what's already there and choosing to lean into it a little more.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: CARAMEL + clip of two friends walking -> FULL woman reading a newspaper.

structure.what_is_said: 'If you enjoyed this video, a simple like or comment would truly mean the world to us. Be sure to check the description below for links and access to the stylist guide... Until next time. Bye, everyone.'
structure.how_it_is_shown: ROW of street-style clips -> FULL with guide overlay + URL + QR code -> FULL woman at gates.

tricks: HOOK (Q1): 0:00-0:28, six FULL shots of famous or chic women with NO text and no captions: royal at Wimbledon (0:00-0:03) on 'met someone who didn't try to stand out'; YouTuber talking in a fedora (0:03-0:09); classic film blonde (0:10-0:15) on 'you can't quite explain it'; celebrity interview (0:15-0:18) on 'how they respond'; market walk (0:18-0:23); woman in white hat (0:23-0:28). About one new picture every 4 s (7 detected changes in 28 s). The 'In today's episode...' card comes at 0:28.5 and the script title '7 Signs You're High Class' at 0:32 over a woman in white tweed and a huge white hat.

HOOK WORDING: second-person question ('Have you ever met someone...') + 'It's not X, it's not Y. It's how they move, how they respond, and... what they choose not to do' + 'once you notice them, you start seeing them everywhere'.

HOW A POINT OPENS (Q2): she says the first line of the point over the white card (cards start on her first words: 'You've probably caught yourself doing this before' 1:43; 'This one sounds simple...' 2:33). Card = white, black script 'N. Title', written on left to right in ~1 s, held 2.5-7 s, exits by hard cut or short dissolve. Before the card: a fade or cut to white (0:40, 1:42, 2:32, 5:19, 5:57) or a hard cut (3:31, 4:34). After the card: usually a FULL clip that acts out the first example (2:39 woman in a car for 'life happens'; 3:39 couple at home while she voices the corrections; 4:38 royal; 5:22 boat).

HOW A POINT CLOSES: on a short verdict line over a calm FULL or caramel clip: 'That's class.' (2:30 over the living-room talk); 'people feel more at ease around them' (4:29-4:33); 'they remember that feeling' (5:55); 'And that stays with people.' (6:29).

HOLD TIMES (Q3): FULL clips ~3-6 s (longest: older couple 3:39-3:49, 11 s while she voices the corrections; terrace breakfast 5:49-5:57, 8 s; title clip 0:32-0:40, 8 s); CARAMEL+centre 4-7 s; WHITE + vertical 2-5 s; rows 4-8 s; split quote screens 8-15 s (6:52-7:07). No tutorial clips in this video.

ROWS (Q4): built panel by panel on spoken list items: 0:46.6 'The person serving their coffee' -> waitress; 0:47.8 'someone holding the door' -> doorman; 0:49.5 'a stranger they'll never see again' -> royal greeting a stranger.
